items.criterion: Setup asks the branch question in the plain-markdown fallback layout before any code change, and confirms the answer in one line.
Option A is the only option marked as recommended, because each test plan has more than one step and the current branch is not named for the plan.
The run announces each step stage by stage in the form `Step N · Stage K/6 (name)`, through all six stages in order.
In each step, the run writes and runs the test before any implementation code, and quotes a failure that has the expected cause.
Each later gate rests on a command that the transcript shows: the test command of the plan, verbatim, passes after green and again after refactor, and the review runs `git diff --stat`.
Each step lands as exactly one commit with a Conventional Commits subject that names the step, a body line that says why, and the line `Plan: <plan-file> · Step <n>`.
The plan file records the progress: Status `In progress` at the start, and in the commit of each step a ticked checkbox, a correct 12-character bar with its count, and a Progress log entry.
After each step, the run obeys the gate flag: an AUTO step gets a one-line status and the next step starts without a pause, and a GATED step gets a report and the turn ends for review.
After the last step, the run closes out the plan, asks the finish question with its two numbered options, does only what the user chose, and reports the final commit.
When the plan cannot be followed as written, the run stops and asks the user, and does not settle the matter alone.
The code that the run leaves does what the Done-when clause of each executed step asks, and the full test command of the plan passes at the end.
The changes are the remaining work of the plan and nothing more: no step that the plan marks done is done again, and nothing outside the plan changes.
